definition: Depth and durability of published scientific evidence for the mechanism family.
Evidence across independent samples, markets, authors, and time periods.
Maturity of explanatory theories and known failure modes.
Clarity of the proposed behavioral/risk/institutional mechanism.
Ability to transform the mechanism into a precise research construct.
Ability to express the construct deterministically without model discretion.
Availability of point-in-time or reproducible public data.
Compatibility with long-only equity research without requiring short portfolios.
Risk that implementation requires information unavailable at decision time.
Expected sensitivity to arbitrary thresholds or narrow parameter choices.
Strength of evidence outside original samples or definitions.
Expected scientific information gain for MEDP.
Expected conceptual information beyond validated risk constructs, without claiming proven independence.
Potential to integrate later with risk constructs while preserving phase boundaries.
